keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page gives 14,496 km2; the gazetteer's modern departments of Bas-Rhin, Haut-Rhin and Moselle come to about 14,415 km2 (ratio 0.99), so the region is exact in extent. Belfort stayed French ('Territoire de Belfort, made a full departement in 1922').

ledger.note: 28 June 1871: the German Empire creates the Imperial Territory of Alsace-Lorraine. 'the Imperial Territory was created on 28 June 1871', at first 'administered directly by an imperial governor appointed by Wilhelm I'; France had ceded it by the Treaty of Frankfurt signed 10 May 1871 (see the Treaty page: 'except for the city of Belfort and its territory').

ledger.note: November 1918: France takes Alsace-Lorraine back. 'The German troops left between 16 and 20 November. French troops entered Strasbourg on 22 November, and the Nationalrat proclaimed annexation to France on 5 December.' Recognised by the Treaty of Versailles in 1919 (the page's lead says 1920).

ledger.note: 1918: the Reichsland ends. Councils formed in Mulhouse, Colmar and Strasbourg; the German troops left 16-20 November 1918; Alsace-Lorraine passes to the French Third Republic.

wars.outcome: German victory: Sedan (1-2 September 1870), Paris armistice (January 1871) and the Treaty of Frankfurt of 10 May 1871, by which France ceded Alsace (except Belfort) and most of Lorraine's Moselle ('the ceding of 1,694 French villages and cities to Germany') and owed five billion francs; German occupation of parts of France ended in September 1873.
wars.note: Franco-Prussian War page: war declared 19 July 1870; Sedan 1-2 September; Metz surrendered 26 October 1870; Paris fell 28 January 1871; 'most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine ... became the Imperial Territory of Alsace-Lorraine'.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Frankfurt fixed the frontier village by village (1,694 villages and towns); Belfort, kept by France, is the exception that makes the line.

notes: New dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks: the Imperial Territory (Reichsland) of Alsace-Lorraine, 1871-1918, held directly by the German Empire (type 'state' because it had its own territory, capital and, from 1911, a constitution and parliament; the renderer may prefer a lighter tint of german-empire). Counterparts french-third-republic (Cliopatria row, dossier not yet written at my run) and german-empire (Cliopatria row) must carry the matching loss/gain at 1871/5-6 and 1918/11. The page is inconsistent on the final cession (lead 1920, body 1919 Treaty of Versailles); the dossier ends in November 1918 when German rule ended, while Cliopatria's French Third Republic shape grows only from 1919. The page gives no Statthalter list (table empty), so no rulers strip. Not opened for lack of budget: the Zabern affair page, the 1911 constitution, the World War I fighting in Alsace (1914-18). The 1874 Landesausschuss (29 Oct 1874), the 1879 Reichsstatthalter and the 1911 constitution (31 May 1911) are governance changes with no ledger type. The Saales and Schirmeck cantons (from Vosges) lie in the modern Bas-Rhin, so the department union is exact.
